issues.description: The central blue hollow ladder (make_duplex at y=0, x 0.55-6.0) is disconnected from both templates (y=±1.35) and reads as a third, additional DNA molecule, not unreplicated parental duplex. Templates are fully separated across the whole frame from t=0, the fork never advances, and both new strands are built right of the fork line over this ladder; lagging fragments therefore grow toward the fork. Parental body is unregistered, so identity cannot be confirmed.

artifact_evidence.observation: Three parallel blue bodies: upper line, lower line, and a separate hollow rung ladder between them starting at the vertical fork line; no convergence of templates into the ladder.

issues.description: The polymerase extending the continuous leading strand is labeled 'Pol δ'. Per F4 the bulk of leading-strand synthesis at an undisturbed eukaryotic fork is Pol ε; Pol δ is the lagging-strand elongation/maturation enzyme (F6). The same cyan asset/label is reused for leading, lagging and fill, misassigning enzyme identity on the leading strand.

artifact_evidence.observation: Cyan clamp-shaped enzyme labeled 'Pol δ' sits at the rightward-growing green leading strand on the upper template.

issues.description: After primer removal and right-to-left gap fill (fill spans x≈2.0-2.55), the red nick and ligase seal are placed at x=2.55, while fragment-2 DNA begins at x≈2.86. A visible gap remains between the sealed 'nick' and the downstream fragment, so ligase appears to seal a position where no adjacent 3'-OH/5'-P ends meet. Order (remove→fill→nick→ligase) is correct, but the seal geometry is not a true nick.

artifact_evidence.observation: Gold ligase over a red mark between the filled green segment and the next green-orange fragment, with empty template space still visible to the right of the mark.

checks.reason: Primer fade precedes fill; fill adds right-to-left (2.46→2.27→2.09) matching lower-template 5'→3' reading; ligase acts only after fill, adds no DNA.
Static fork, fully separated templates, and disconnected central ladder make parental vs extra DNA ambiguous; synthesis occurs over the ladder region.
Leading enzyme labeled Pol δ contradicts F4 (Pol ε model).
Seal position leaves a residual gap; not a junction of adjacent ends.
